# Independent audit: signed complete cuts and actual isolated facets

Audit target:
`candidate 2951c303a65db1e9`,
Sections 1--6. Verdict: PASS, with the stated completeness, convexity,
and actual two-direction isolation hypotheses retained. No correction found.

## Complete signed paths

Completeness is needed separately for every action and every sampled
fiber/normal. It makes the zero-time sampled fibers exact and supplies
an active cut at every old normal. No intersection with the old body and
no zero augmentation may be inserted when fields can be negative.

The global finite convex fields have uniform affine lower growth on the
compact base/normal parameter set. The radial inequality therefore bounds
the entire new ambient set, not only a preselected neighborhood. After
this bound, all fields have a uniform absolute bound. Completeness gives
the outer parallel-body bound and old inner homothet. Thus sampled fibers
are positive, uniformly O(t) close and radially O(t) close, and convexity
preserves every actual anchored inclusion. The optional deficient-rank
repair preserves the integer fibers; no false containment in the original
ambient body is used.

At a regular boundary point, an old active cut gives the lower radial
speed bound. Compactness of the finite-index/unit-normal family gives a
new active cut at the new radial endpoint. Its old slack is nonnegative
and O(t); every subsequential limit is an old active cut with the unique
old supporting normal. Dividing by the positive radial support distance
gives the matching upper bound, including negative speeds. The resulting
speed is exactly the active maximum, without a positive part.

## Actual addition and responses

Every composite baseline uses strictly positive weights. Its zero slack
is equivalent to simultaneous zero slack of all components. Since each
component active set is nonempty, the maximum of the independently indexed
sum is the sum of the component maxima. Coefficients of fields may vanish;
baseline weights must not. This is one actual compatible signed path, not
Minkowski interpolation of new bodies.

Bounded signed radial shell expansions consequently add total, energy,
covariance, and regular fixed-cap first responses. Supporting cap responses
are correctly excluded: their positive-part terms need the actual summed
speed in the separately audited directional-inverse theorem. The printed
interval example has the correct nonadditivity signs.

## Isolated facet

Both directions of the forced-contact exclusion are necessary in the
argument. The source-p plane must be inactive at all other sampled bases,
and all other source planes must be inactive at p. The selected forced-only
slopes are continuous, so these finitely many strict gaps persist on a
normal neighborhood. A normal cutoff then isolates the single facet
normal of the polytope K_p. Other sampled fibers have a zero active speed;
other facets of K_p have zero cutoff; their joins are surface-null.

The choices phi=1, phi=-1 and phi=-T, with T the concave pyramid tent,
are genuinely finite convex fields after extension off the facet. Their
nonnegative finite combinations remain convex and are realized by the
same complete baselines. This verifies the physical feasibility needed
for the free-facet curvature argument, but only under the actual
isolation premise. No arbitrary contact-constrained facet is presumed free.

The final comparison with the older potential cone is appropriately
limited: on a common compact neighborhood, a large constant makes a
signed convex field nonnegative; the compensating global constant is
an affine signed speed. The old penalty approximation controls fixed
responses and strict improvement, not exact neutral faces.

## Verification

Independently reran
`supporting computation verify_signed_global_cut_addition_defect_transport.py`:
911 exact signed-cut/actual-interval checks PASS.
The geometric compactness and contact arguments above are independently
read proofs; the finite checker is supplementary.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
